chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Wanting to be an artist; moving from drums to other instruments
summary: Spikes wanted to be a cartoonist; after Johnny bought him drums he moved to saxophone, trumpet, clarinet and bass, and stopped playing in 1936.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Uh, after your brother came back...uh, is that when you started getting involved in music? Is that right?

Yeah. I had never tried to be a musician. I wanted to be an artist. I used to could draw anything with either hand. Any time they in school they wanted something put on the blackboard or anything, I always would...could draw, you know, and print. Now, just like you see that boy there, Simi, done all that stuff. I can do that--all that stuff. Uh, uh..uh, uh, I've always wanted to be an artist, you know, and my mother worked for a guy that was a... in The Examiner in the cartoon department. He want me to come work with him but I didn't go to work. My brother come home, why they all ...everybody was musicians but me. So he come home and bought me a set of drums and took me back with him, and that started it. I went from drums to saxophone and from saxophone to trumpet and trumpet to
clarinet, and then I got so I could play bass viol, you know. I played all the brass instruments.
Which saxophone did you start with? Which kind of a saxophone was first?
Oh, I started with the alto sax. That's what almost everybody starts with, you know. A lot of people like tenor. I never did play tenor.
Played baritone and alto, and I played soprano. I got soprano, alto...I got a gold alto up there. I betcha could get some money for it 'cause it's about sixty years old.
You ever play any instrument any more?
No, I haven't touched it since '35...'36. '36!
